doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Asking Coltrane and Jimmy Garrison about their approach
summary: At the Village Vanguard he talked about reeds with Coltrane and could get nothing explanatory from Garrison.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Yeah, those things were happening, yeah, a little bit. I remember being down at the Village Vanguard and thinking, that was me, I mean knew me, John Coltrane, and I was to him about reeds backstage and he was trying different reeds, this doesn’t work, that doesn’t work, and I asked Jimmy Garrison, his bass player, “What are you guys doing with this new thing with McCoy Tyner and everything.” And all he would tell me is “We’re just playing. I mean we’re just doing things we do.” I mean there wasn’t any secret that he could tell me like well we’re extending this chord or playing modal. He wouldn’t tell me anything other than we’re just doing our thing. I mean so I couldn’t get any information because I wanted to know what is it that they’re doing that’s so, you know, it was getting further out there and interesting. But I couldn’t really pick up on what they were thinking about when they were doing this.
Either he didn’t want to give away any secrets, or maybe they were just doing that.
Yeah, they were just doing that without thinking like well we’re doing this and that’s why we’re —
Yeah, that’s why it sounds like it does.
Yeah. So I think no one, I mean whoever was, I think I mentioned Jimmy Garrison, I’m not sure who else I spoke to.
